senses.gloss: The level or point at which something begins to happen or take effect.
senses.ru: порог, предел (уровень, с которого что-л. начинается)
examples: Her income is just above the *threshold* for financial aid.
Everyone has a different pain *threshold*.
Sales have to cross a certain *threshold* before the bonus kicks in.

senses.gloss: The nail on a person's thumb.
examples: He chewed his *thumbnail* while the results loaded.
I split my *thumbnail* prying open the box.
She scraped the price sticker off with her *thumbnail*.

senses.gloss: The future.
examples: These students are the leaders of *tomorrow*.
The whole exhibit was about the city of *tomorrow*.
He spends money like there's no *tomorrow*.

senses.gloss: The moment when an aircraft or spacecraft lands.
examples: The lander sent back photos minutes after *touchdown*.
We felt a hard bump at *touchdown*.
The crew announced *touchdown* at 6:15 local time.

senses.gloss: A habit, feature, or style so typical of one person or group that everyone recognizes it.
examples: That sly grin was his *trademark*.
Long guitar solos became the band's *trademark*.
Showing up ten minutes late is her *trademark*.

senses.gloss: A move of a person from one place, job, school, or team to another.
senses.ru: перевод (на другую работу, в другую школу, в другой клуб)
examples: He put in for a *transfer* to the Denver office.
Her *transfer* to the day shift comes through in March.
Two of the team's starters asked for *transfers*.

senses.gloss: A ticket that lets a passenger change to another bus or train without paying again.
examples: Ask the driver for a *transfer* when you get on.
My *transfer* expired before the second bus showed up.
One fare includes two free *transfers*.

senses.gloss: Openness about how decisions are made and money is spent.
examples: Voters are demanding more *transparency* from city hall.
The company promised full *transparency* about the layoffs.
There is very little *transparency* in how the grants are awarded.

senses.gloss: A person who has moved from another part of the country to live somewhere new.
examples: As a New York *transplant*, he still can't get used to the quiet.
Half the neighborhood is *transplants* from California.
The town has filled up with *transplants* since the plant opened.

senses.gloss: A ship, plane, or truck used to carry troops or supplies.
examples: The troops flew home on a military *transport*.
A cargo *transport* touched down just before dawn.
The wounded were loaded onto a *transport* headed for the base.

senses.gloss: A dull, exhausting routine that never seems to lead anywhere.
examples: He quit his job to get off the corporate *treadmill*.
Grading papers every weekend felt like a *treadmill*.
Once you're on the debt *treadmill*, it's hard to step off.

senses.gloss: A person or thing that is greatly loved and valued.
examples: Our librarian is a real *treasure*.
That old photo album is a family *treasure*.
The town considers the little theater one of its *treasures*.

senses.gloss: The way someone or something is dealt with or behaved toward.
examples: The workers complained about unfair *treatment*.
The book's *treatment* of the war is surprisingly gentle.
Guests get the same *treatment* whether they're famous or not.

senses.gloss: A process in which something is cleaned, protected, or given new properties.
examples: The city's water *treatment* plant runs around the clock.
The deck needs a *treatment* of sealant every spring.
Heat *treatments* make the steel much harder.

senses.gloss: A percussion instrument made of a bent steel bar, struck with a metal stick.
examples: She played the *triangle* in the school orchestra.
You can hear the *triangle* ringing over the strings.
The music teacher handed out tambourines and *triangles*.

senses.gloss: The practice of posting deliberately offensive or provocative messages online to upset people.
examples: The comment section was shut down because of constant *trolling*.
She reported him for *trolling* and blocked the account.
Half of what he posts is just *trolling*.

senses.gloss: A period of confusion, conflict, or sudden change in a situation.
examples: The company survived a year of financial *turbulence*.
There was real political *turbulence* after the vote.
The family went through some *turbulence* after the move.

senses.gloss: A small folded pastry with fruit sealed inside.
examples: She warmed up an apple *turnover* for breakfast.
The bakery makes a good peach *turnover* in the summer.
He ate half a cherry *turnover* and left the rest.

senses.gloss: A play in which a team loses the ball to the other side.
examples: The defense forced a *turnover* on the very first drive.
That *turnover* in the fourth quarter cost them the game.
He scored sixteen points with only one *turnover*.

senses.gloss: The flat spinning platform of a record player, or the player itself.
examples: He set the needle down gently on the *turntable*.
She bought a *turntable* and started collecting records again.
The DJ worked two *turntables* and a mixer.

senses.gloss: A greenish-blue color.
examples: The water in the cove was a brilliant *turquoise*.
The walls were painted a soft *turquoise*.
She picked *turquoise* for the bridesmaids' dresses.

senses.gloss: The last stage of something, when it is fading or coming to an end.
examples: He hit thirty home runs in the *twilight* of his career.
The novel is set in the *twilight* of the Roman Empire.
In the *twilight* of her life she took up painting.

senses.gloss: Sound waves pitched too high for people to hear.
examples: Bats find their way in the dark using *ultrasound*.
The jeweler cleans rings with *ultrasound*.
*Ultrasound* travels well through water.

senses.gloss: A single organization or term that covers many smaller groups or parts.
examples: The clinic works under the *umbrella* of the state health department.
Six local clubs now meet under one *umbrella*.
The phrase serves as an *umbrella* for several different conditions.

senses.gloss: An informal agreement between people.
examples: We have an *understanding* about who pays for what.
They reached an *understanding* after two hours of talks.
There's an unwritten *understanding* that nobody parks in that spot.

senses.gloss: Money paid by the government to someone who has lost a job.
examples: He filed for *unemployment* the day after the layoff.
She's been living on *unemployment* since March.
*Unemployment* runs out after twenty-six weeks in most states.

senses.gloss: A particular world of activity, or the whole imagined world of a story.
examples: The show takes place in the same *universe* as the comics.
In the *universe* of college sports, that's a huge salary.
The two movies belong to completely different *universes*.

senses.gloss: Official permission to do something that local zoning or building rules do not normally allow.
senses.ru: разрешение на отступление от норм (застройки, зонирования)
examples: They needed a *variance* to build the garage that close to the property line.
The zoning board denied the *variance*.
The restaurant finally got a *variance* for its outdoor seating.
